text: {"score":3,"justification":"Headline and numbers are accurate and the cautious 'inconclusive' leaning fits the thin records. But the narrative has several claims that don't fit the card, and the next steps are generic and do not follow the narrative's own recommendation.","problems":["Narrative says the elevated 99215 share 'appears in every complexity band'; the card supports this (all bands exceed all-provider share), but the claim is weakly stated and the 3+ bands have tiny n.","Says 'often for simple presentations such as abdominal pain, UTI, rash or back pain' - dx codes support R10.9, N39.0, M54.50, but R21 (rash) is fine; the characterization of UTI from N39.0 is an inference not labeled as such.","Cited examples C0218631, C0218674, C0218821 are consistent with low complexity, but C0218626 and C0218846 are called 'plausible' high-complexity 99215s without documentation evidence.","Says 'The claims pattern points toward upcoding' while leaning is 'inconclusive' and headline says cannot confirm; mixed tone.","Says C0218610 'deserves scrutiny for cloned or inflated notes' - speculative; no evidence of cloning in the packet.","Says 99214 unsupported rate 'noticeably above' comparison on 3 of 18 claims (16.7% vs 3.3%) - small sample, though caveated.","Next steps are generic: narrative says to request full charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims but next_steps only say to request a larger sample and re-screen; no specific claim IDs named.","Cited claim C0218614 has no documentation and is cited only as an example, adding little support; 'Of 3 documented 99215 claims' only two examples shown, the third not identified."]}
